newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar climbs as high as 127.10 yen after G7.
newsitem.headline: Dollar climbs as high as 127.10 yen after G7.

text.p: *Dollar climbed as high as 127.10 yen in early Tokyo after G7 statements on currencies were not as strong as anticipated and failed to refer to dollar/yen rate directly.
*The dollar rose as high as 1.7390 marks in early Tokyo trading, its highest level since February 1994.

*Interbank traders seen main force behind dollar's rise, although some Japanese investors such as trust banks also riding on move, dealers said. Option-linked stop-loss dollar buying expected to emerge at 127.30 yen, although clear break of that point could strengthen fears of BOJ's intervention.

*Dealers said dollar likely to test this year's high of 127.16 yen in near term. "The G7 was considered somewhat of a turning point for the dollar rally, but in fact the lack of strong remarks on the dollar/yen would open the way for it (the dollar) to rise to 130 yen," said a senior Japanese trader.
*Dollar retreated slightly due to sales by exporters and profit-taking after touching this morning's highs.
*Dollar eased on media report that Bundesbank's chief Hans Tietmeyer said: "We are not seeking a weak yen but a strong yen". Tietmeyer also said U.S. wanted strong dollar but not stronger dollar.
*Dollar held on to its early gains in early Asian trading after Group of Seven (G7) meeting. Dollar rose more than 0.70 yen and quoted at 126.83/88 yen at 2220 GMT.
*Dollar was bought as G7 failed specifically to mention "yen's weakness" as shared concern.
*But in joint communique G7 stressed need to avoid currency rates that spur trade imbalances, which indirectly referred to yen and Japan's rising trade surplus.
*G7 also said its members will cooperate as appropriate in foreign exchange markets.
*Market appears ready to drive dollar higher to test if Bank of Japan will step in to cap further advance of dollar.
*Dollar may be pushed up to 127.16 yen, a four year and eight month high, set on April 10 in Tokyo.
*Buying was led by inter-bank traders. Dollar ended New York at 126.20/30 on Friday.
*Dollar also higher against mark, reflecting its rise against yen.
*Dollar quoted at 1.7315/25 marks at 2224 GMT, compared with New York close of 1.7255/65 marks on Friday.
